title: Quarterly corridor & contingency blueprint for Hosted API + Model Catalog
creator: Marisol Chen
description: Purpose: Create a concise, operational blueprint that defines the quarterly 'corridor' (allowed commit windows, model rotation lanes, and hedges) for Hosted API + Model Catalog releases, plus explicit contingency actions for capacity, model quality regressions, and SLA stress. Scope: - Define three commitment lanes (Green: low-risk, Amber: monitored, Red: conservative) for model onboarding and hosted endpoint changes. - Establish canary and shadow traffic experiment patterns tied to model health signals. - Define capacity hedges (dedicated buffer, cross-region spillover) and automatic fallback policy mapping. - Produce rollout matrix (owner, SLO rollback thresholds, test suites, monitoring dashboards) and integration checklist for engineering, infra, DX, and CS teams. Out of scope: changes to pricing/tokens, deep model architecture evaluation (handled by Research), or on-prem packaging specifics. Rationale: Past quarters saw surprise regressions during rotation weeks with limited guardrails. This blueprint aims to reduce outage risk and enable more predictable quarterly commits while keeping runway for experiments.
acceptance_criteria: Corridor document published in Confluence with decision matrix and lane definitions
Automated canary policy templates added to the rollout repo (PR merged)
3 example model onboarding playbooks (one per lane) with test and monitoring checks
SLO-driven rollback thresholds and alert runbooks validated with SRE and Product
Runbook tabletop exercise completed with cross-functional participants and notes captured
